name: adjacency
method:
for each entry point, the call closure (srcindex.Resolver, at most DEPTH hops and
NODE_CAP functions) is walked and every reached function contributes
  - SQL effects of its SQL text: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE/DDL targets are writes, FROM/JOIN are reads, with the
    hints %NOLOCK/%NOINDEX/%NOCHECK/FOR UPDATE and SQL transaction statements;
  - ObjectScript global references classified by command (Set target, Kill, $Increment, Merge target = write;
    otherwise read), LOCK commands with mode and timeout, TSTART/TCOMMIT/TROLLBACK (with or without a level), $TLevel;
  - Python Native API global access and WriteTxn / commit / rollback markers;
  - implicit server hooks the SQL filer runs for a write: the functional indexes idx_edges_adj (Graph.KG.AdjIndex ->
    Graph.KG.Adjacency) on Graph_KG.rdf_edges and idx_labels_adj (Graph.KG.LabelIndex) on Graph_KG.rdf_labels
    (iris_vector_graph/schema.py:774-780), and the iFind index on rdf_props.val / docs.text (schema.py:482, 566).
Every item keeps up to MAX_AT source locations with the function it came from. Records carry
`confidence: "extracted"`; entries listed in footprint_reviews.json are merged with the reviewer's corrections and
marked `confidence: "reviewed"`. `journal` stays null here: the lane fills it from the journal oracle.
Known limits: string-built SQL whose table name is a runtime value is reported as Graph_KG.<dynamic:...>; dynamic
dispatch (getattr, callbacks) is not followed; a Set whose target is computed by indirection is caught only through
$Name; Python helpers reached through a variable are missed. The reviewed subset corrects what was checked by hand.

atomicity_claim.claim: the cache entry is never wrongly current (generation-validated cache)

notes: F-0401: soundness needs every writer to move gen after its change; RemoveSource/RemoveGraph/RemoveAll kill it (back to 0) and FillEdge refills without stepping

journal.transaction_note: Adj.Degree stores ^KG('degc') (a reader that writes), no transaction.

writes.global:^KG(\"degc\", g, s, key): Set $ListBuild(gen, count) when the probe was granted, no ^IVG.AdjNoLock(g), and the generation did not move; Kill if it moved right after

review.transactions: none (reader); a <PROTECT> on the store is swallowed (read-only login)
review.locks: probe LOCK +^IVG.AdjW(g)#"E":0, released at once when granted (Adj.cls:68-72)

atomicity_claim.claim: Every adjacency write must bump the generation and hold the shared lock

notes: $Increment of gen/__version is not undone by a rollback (P-0401): see F-0402

writes.global:^IVG.AdjNoLock(g): $Increment when the writer lock is not granted in 5 s (WriterLock)
writes.global:^NKG: only when ^NKG("$meta","nodeCount") exists (interning via GraphIndex, under LOCK ^NKG)

review.transactions: none of its own: runs in the caller's transaction (row hook: the row's)
review.locks: LOCK +^IVG.AdjW(g)#"S":5, released right after the writes (Lock:tLocked -...#"S"); inside a transaction the release is deferred to its end (P-0003); GraphIndex.InternNode LOCK +^NKG (no timeout)

notes: F-0405: a weight change on an existing leaf moves neither gen nor the graph-version token

journal.transaction_note: PutShadow called with no caller transaction: out/in written outside any transaction (by design of the call).

writes.global:^KG(\"gen\")/(\"__version\"): $Increment ONLY when the leaf did not exist

notes: F-0201: with the mode off one unkeyed leaf stands for the triple; Remove kills it whichever row went

writes.global:^NKG: GraphIndex.DeleteIndex when no other graph holds the triple

notes: F-0401: Kill ^KG("gen", g) resets every source generation to 0 instead of stepping it; a reader that read generation 0 earlier can store a count as current

review.locks: LOCK +^IVG.AdjW(g)#"S":5, error when not granted; released at the end

atomicity_claim.claim: Every adjacency write must bump the generation and hold the shared lock

notes: F-0407: no writer lock and no generation step, against the ADR's literal rule (harmless for counts)

journal.transaction_note: Reweight: out/in/__version, no lock, no generation (F-0407).

writes.global:^KG(\"out\"/\"in\"): Set weight where the leaf exists

review.locks: none (deliberately: comment at 327; LOCK_EXEMPT_METHODS in tests/unit/test_degree_cache_writers.py)

transactions.marker: TRollback  [no level: rolls back every level, P-0409]

atomicity_claim.claim: An IVG write never commits or rolls back a transaction its caller opened

notes: F-0409: TRollback without a level at TraversalBuild.cls:156 (file line) discards a caller's open work when sync() runs in the caller's process (engine on a DB-API connection, not from_connect)
candidate (HD-0402): two rebuilds (sync, rebuild_kg, a second BuildKG) both get the shared parent lock and run at once; nothing makes a rebuild exclusive

writes.indexed namespace: %BuildIndices of idxedgesadj and idxlabelsadj (TraversalBuild.cls:88-91) -> AdjIndex.PurgeIndex (Adjacency.RemoveAll) + InsertIndex per row
writes.non-indexed namespace: Kill ^KG("label"), Adjacency.RemoveAll, then FillEdge per row and ^KG("label") per label row

review.transactions: TStart (TraversalBuild.cls:40), TCommit then TStart every 50,000 rows (121), TCommit (125); on error 'If $TLevel > 0 { TRollback }' with NO level (156): rolls back every level, the caller's included (P-0409). Outside a caller transaction the rebuild is committed in 50,000-row pieces
review.locks: Adjacency.BeginRebuild: LOCK +^IVG.AdjW#"S":5 on the PARENT name in SHARED mode (Adjacency.cls:814-822), held to EndRebuild: it blocks the readers' exclusive child probes (P-0404) but not another rebuild

journal.explanation: TraversalBuild.BuildKG rebuilds the functional indexes with %BuildIndices (iris_src/src/Graph/KG/TraversalBuild.cls:126-131), which writes the index storage of rdf_edges and rdf_labels; with 8 parallel jobs (the journal shows two other server processes) and after BuildKG's TCommit, so the ^KG refill is journaled outside any transaction, as the method's own comment says (TraversalBuild.cls:55-65, 150-158: a failed rebuild has already shown readers a partial ^KG).

review.transactions: three separate class-method calls through self._iris_obj() (iris_vector_graph/engine.py:1894-1942): the cursor's own process when the engine was built on a DB-API connection, but a second DB-API connection (another server process) on an engine made by from_connect (connection params with a username); no caller-transaction refusal (unlike initialize_schema 2148-2156)
